en.title: Global expansion persists, but growth is fragmenting and credit is getting more expensive
en.deck: November flash PMIs keep major economies in expansion but reveal a wider gap across regions; high-yield spreads, emerging-market outflows and energy logistics show why an equity rebound is not broad financial easing.
en.regime: Global activity remains expansionary in several major economies, but regional dispersion is widening while credit risk premia and emerging-market financing conditions remain restrictive.
en.key_risk: A renewed Gulf shipping disruption combined with wider high-yield spreads and persistent emerging-market outflows could transmit a regional slowdown into broader investment and employment weakness.

pt-BR.title: A expansão global persiste, mas o crescimento se fragmenta e o crédito encarece
pt-BR.deck: Os PMIs preliminares de novembro mantêm as principais economias em expansão, mas revelam uma distância maior entre regiões; spreads de high yield, saídas de emergentes e logística energética mostram por que a recuperação das bolsas não equivale a alívio financeiro amplo.
pt-BR.regime: A atividade global permanece expansionista em várias economias importantes, mas a dispersão regional aumenta enquanto os prêmios de risco de crédito e as condições de financiamento dos emergentes seguem restritivos.
pt-BR.key_risk: Uma nova interrupção marítima no Golfo, combinada a spreads high yield mais amplos e saídas persistentes dos mercados emergentes, pode transmitir uma desaceleração regional para o investimento e o emprego em escala maior.

signal_rationale.delta: The 23 November edition focused on China's iron-ore/steel chain and exporter inventories; the 22 November edition examined AI productivity and valuation; the 21 November edition covered cross-asset repricing. This edition adds a distinct cross-region activity signal from the 23–24 November flash PMIs and connects it to credit spreads, October emerging-market flows, the 23 November oil close and Brazil's newly published macrofiscal parameter revision.
signal_rationale.evidence: November composite PMIs: US 54.6, euro area 51.7, Germany 55.0, France 46.2, UK 52.3, Japan 51.5 and India 56.3. US high-yield OAS widened from 3.23% on 13 Nov to 3.76% on 20 Nov. IIF estimated US$33.8bn of EM portfolio outflows in October. Brent settled at US$89.37/bbl on 23 Nov while IEA estimated October supply at 105.4 mb/d and inventories +52m barrels. Brazil’s 2027 GDP assumption was revised from 2.3% to 1.8%, and IPCA from 3.8% to 4.5%. The 23 Nov Brazil Focus survey raised the 2026 exchange-rate median from R$5.40 to R$5.55, raised IPCA from 5.11% to 5.15% and cut GDP growth from 1.72% to 1.70%. AP reported that Nvidia's board reinstated CEO Jensen Huang amid an investigation into possible foreign-spy and national-security concerns; Nvidia shares rose 31.5% on 23 November, a company-specific catalyst behind the technology concentration in the equity rebound.
signal_rationale.scale_path: Regional survey dispersion changes expected revenue, hiring and inventory paths; those differences shape central-bank decisions, sovereign yields and currency conditions; higher credit premia and cross-border outflows then affect investment and procurement, while crude, refined products and freight transmit energy shocks into prices and margins.
signal_rationale.transmission: PMI divergence -> sector revenue and labour demand -> domestic inflation and monetary policy -> yields, FX and refinancing costs -> portfolio flows and investment. Oil supply and shipping -> crude and refined-product prices -> transport, food and industrial costs -> inflation expectations and policy reaction.
signal_rationale.falsifier: The thesis weakens if the Germany–France PMI gap narrows materially, US high-yield spreads reverse the November widening, non-resident EM portfolio flows return to positive territory, refined-product premiums decline broadly and subsequent national-accounts data show no meaningful regional output or employment divergence.

key_constraints: Flash PMIs are diffusion surveys, not GDP growth rates or official output data; country readings are not a direct measure of the size of output gaps.
The US high-yield OAS series ends on 20 November at the cutoff; it is not a 23 November market close and covers a US dollar-denominated below-investment-grade bond index rather than all credit.
IIF portfolio flows are October monthly estimates, not daily November flows.
The Brazil Ministry of Finance parameter grid was closed on 6 November; it is a forecast vintage, not a realised outcome or market-consensus survey.
FAO’s food-price index is an international commodity basket, not a retail-price or household-affordability measure; the latest meat component mixes projected and observed prices and can be revised.

Reports of attacks and statements by the Houthi movement, Bahrain, Iran and UKMTO are attributed to the relevant actors or reporting institution; the available material does not quantify a new sustained loss of oil output.
The October global crude-steel release had not been located by the 05:00 BRT cutoff; September remains the latest complete global comparison.
The US Treasury par curve is nominal and does not separately identify expected inflation, real-rate expectations and term premium.
The 23 November Brazil Focus medians are market expectations for 2026 reported by B3; they are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's 2027 parameter grid.

producer_checks.novelty_decision: Distinct regional-activity and financing-dispersion thesis; does not repeat the preceding cross-asset selloff, AI productivity/valuation or China iron-ore/steel-chain theses.

reproducibility_notes.pmi_comparison: Flash composite PMI output indices published 23–24 Nov 2026; 50 is the expansion/contraction threshold. The values are survey diffusion indices, not GDP growth rates.
reproducibility_notes.credit_spread: ICE BofA US High Yield Index OAS via FRED, unit Percent: 3.23% on 13 Nov; 3.34% on 16 Nov; 3.43% on 17 Nov; 3.47% on 18 Nov; 3.52% on 19 Nov; 3.76% on 20 Nov. Latest observation available at the 05:00 BRT cutoff.
reproducibility_notes.treasury_curve: US Treasury official daily par curve, 23 Nov 2026: 2-year 4.63%; 10-year 4.92%; 30-year 5.29%.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_forecast: Brazil Ministry of Finance November 2026 Macrofiscal Bulletin, summary p.3 and detailed grid discussion p.19; grid closed 6 Nov. For 2027, GDP 1.8% (September 2.3%), IPCA 4.5% (3.8%), accumulated Selic 12.93% (12.67%), average exchange rate R$5.34/US$ (R$5.23), and average Brent US$95.20/bbl (US$79.50). The grid's Selic is derived from the real rate implicit in the Focus median (nominal Selic adjusted for market inflation expectations) and converted to nominal terms with the SPE inflation projection; it is distinct from the Focus terminal Selic median of 12.75% at end-2027. FX and Brent are annual averages, not terminal or spot prices.
reproducibility_notes.oil_market: Reuters settlement values for 23 Nov; IEA November report supplies October production and inventory estimates. Spot/futures settlement and monthly supply estimates are different observation types.
reproducibility_notes.food_prices: FAO October 2026 FFPI: 133.9, down 1.2% m/m; cereal 116.8, down 4.5%; sugar 121.3, up 6.6%.
reproducibility_notes.market_flows: IIF tracker published 5 Nov, estimating October non-resident EM portfolio outflows of US$33.8bn; monthly estimate, not daily flow.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_focus: Banco Central do Brasil Focus report with reference date 19 Nov 2026, summarized by B3 on 23 Nov: 2026 GDP 1.70% (from 1.72%), IPCA 5.15% (from 5.11%), and year-end USD/BRL 5.55 (from 5.40). These are market medians, not Central Bank forecasts, and are distinct from the Ministry of Finance's 2027 parameter grid. Primary PDF: https://www.bcb.gov.br/content/focus/focus/R20261119.pdf.
reproducibility_notes.japan_policy: Bank of Japan policy decision published 18 Sep 2026 sets the uncollateralized overnight call-rate guideline around 1.25% and states that the change applies from the next business day, 24 Sep; the October 2026 Outlook Report confirms the level.
reproducibility_notes.brazil_ptax: Banco Central do Brasil PTAX OData historical query for 23 Nov 2026: selling rate 5.97080 at 13:06:23 BRT; date-filtered endpoint retained for reproducibility.

revision_reason: Revision 6 clarifies the Ministry of Finance's 2027 macrofiscal grid: the Selic value is accumulated and derived from the real rate implicit in the Focus median converted with SPE inflation; the exchange-rate and Brent values are annual averages. Both locales and the reproducibility note now distinguish these measures from terminal or spot values.
